subject: Re: Acme DPA redline — retention, subprocessors, and training-rights
content:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme DPA redlines — retention, subprocessors, training rights

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are Acme's initial DPA redlines (v3). Two asks we need to surface before we can move to our legal team sign-off: 1) a 7-year retention carveout for telemetry artifacts related to audit/analytics, 2) an explicit list of subprocessors with runtime export rights called out, and 3) a narrow model-training exception (Acme needs a right to request derivative training on anonymized telemetry).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept those carveouts or propose mitigations? Tom (procurement) will need an estimate on timing for Product/Security approvals — they are hoping to close the contract by end of March.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf

Best,
Sarah Lim
Sr. Contracts Manager
Acme Corporation

-----

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA redlines — retention, subprocessors, training rights

Sarah — thanks for the doc and the clear asks. Looping in Legal (Olga), Security (Aditya) and Product (Karthik) to weigh the technical and compliance impact.

High-level notes up front: we typically push back on long retention windows for telemetry and avoid training exceptions that could expand model IP/derivative rights. Subprocessor disclosure is standard; runtime export rights will need to be scoped carefully.

Olga / Aditya / Karthik — can you review the attached and call out non-starters vs. mitigations we could offer? Acme expects an answer by EOW (3/19). I can prioritize this on the deck.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA redlines — retention, subprocessors, training rights

Kimberly / Sarah — I reviewed Acme's redlines. Summary of redline posture:

- Retention: 7 years for telemetry is a non-standard ask. We can offer up to 24 months for telemetry exports tied to billing/audit, with longer retention only on a per-data-type basis and with documented business justification and indemnities.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide a full list and commit to notice and objection rights for new subprocessors. However, runtime export rights that enable customer-controlled model training need careful IP/usage constraints.
- Training exception: Acme's clause as drafted is broad and could allow model retraining on derived artifacts. Recommend we propose a limited carveout: 1) only on aggregated/anonymized telemetry, 2) explicit prohibition on use to retrain Redwood-owned models or publish derivative models, 3) commercial restrictions (no resale).

Proposed next steps: I can draft counter-language and mark the PDF. If Product confirms technical feasibility for the anonymization boundary and Security signs off on safe export flows, Legal can accept the narrow carveout.

Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: KP_comments_training_clause.docx

-----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA redlines — retention, subprocessors, training rights

Thanks all — technical constraints and notes from Product:

- Telemetry retention: we store request/response traces, KV cache metadata, and operational metrics. Extending retention to 24 months is feasible but has cost and storage implications; we will need a pricing uplift or retention fee. Also need to define which telemetry buckets Acme wants (full request payloads vs. anonymized logs).
- Runtime exports for model training: the runtime currently supports a controlled export path (audit/log export) but not a turnkey dataset generator that strips PII and labels for training. Building an automated anonymization/export pipeline would be ~4-6 weeks of engineering prioritization plus a small infra cost.
- As for prohibitions on retraining: we can enforce via export controls and contract terms, but preventing accidental inclusion in aggregate internal model training requires tagging and internal policy enforcement.

Recommendation: offer a conditional agreement — allow exports of anonymized telemetry for training subject to a one-time engineering integration (scope and cost to be agreed), strict anonymization rules (to be defined), and a contract clause prohibiting use to retrain Redwood models or publish derivatives. Product requests a follow-up call with Acme to define telemetry scope.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA redlines — retention, subprocessors, training rights

Quick security perspective:

- 7-year retention raises exposure risk. If we were to accept longer retention for specific audit artifacts, the data must be encrypted at rest with customer-specific keys (KMS), access controls, and strict role-based access logs (we can provide audit logs).
- Subprocessors: provide the list but add a right to object and a remediation timeline. Any subprocessors with access to raw request/response bodies should be limited and undergo security review or SOC2 evidence.
- Training exports: before allowing any export for training, we need an integration checklist (anonymization proof, schema, sample exports) and a signed runbook describing how exports are produced and validated. If Acme can accept those controls and KMS, Security can sign off.

I can lead the engineering checklist itemization; Product and Legal the anonymization definition.

Aditya Rao
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>, Tom Bates <tbates@acme.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA redlines — retention, subprocessors, training rights

Sarah / Tom — thanks for your patience. Summary and offer from Redwood: 

1) Retention: we cannot accept a blanket 7-year telemetry retention. Offer: up to 24 months retention for telemetry/operational logs tied to billing and audit workflows; for a 7-year retention of specific audit artifacts we can agree on a per-artifact carveout provided Acme funds the extra storage and uses a customer-managed KMS key.

2) Subprocessors: we will provide the current subprocessors list and commit to advance notice (30 days) for new subprocessors. For subprocessors with access to raw request/response bodies, we require a security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence or equivalent.

3) Training/export exception: we can accept a narrow, conditional exception for exports used in Acme's internal model evaluation/training only if ALL of the following are true: (a) exports are limited to aggregated/anonymized telemetry defined by Product, (b) exports occur through a documented, auditable pipeline with KMS-encrypted artifacts, (c) contract language expressly prohibits use to retrain or improve Redwood-owned models or publish derivatives, and (d) Acme signs an export runbook (engineering/scope/cost). Engineering lead time estimated 4-6 weeks; we can provide a SOW/estimate once Acme confirms scope.

Next steps: Olga will send counter-language and mark up Acme_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf. Aditya and Karthik will produce the security checklist and telemetry scope doc. Can Acme confirm whether they will accept the conditional path so we can produce a SOW? If yes, we aim to have marked contract and SOW estimate by COB Monday (3/22).

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments included in thread: Acme_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf, KP_comments_training_clause.docx
